provenance: Computed by the LunarWindow pipeline from NASA LOLA terrain and NASA SPICE (DE421) ephemerides. Code written with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified by the team with automated tests and a comparison against NASA PGDA illumination maps.
verdict: Touchdown 2029-07-24T12 UTC: the Sun's centre is 0.53 deg above the skyline and the top of Earth's disc 0.75 deg above the skyline (power and a link at landing).
Over 14 days: Sun up 95%, Earth in view 94%, both 90% of the time.
Survives the mission: the battery never drops below 140 Wh (lowest 410 Wh).
Longest darkness 14 h: that is the cold soak.
Battery used on this mission: 290 Wh of the 560 Wh it can use above its 140 Wh floor.
Battery model: power = panel power x visible Sun, whatever the Sun's direction (a sun-tracking array), so survival is an upper bound for fixed panels.
why: Darkest spell from 2029-08-05T09 UTC (14 h): terrain 9.8 km away blocks it (bearing 21 deg: skyline 1.41 deg, centre of the body at 1.17 deg).
Longest Earth blackout from 2029-08-06T17 UTC (19 h): it is below the Moon's own curvature (bearing 146 deg, horizon -1.30 deg).

weak_battery.label: assumption: half the battery, e.g. a cell lost or a cold battery

words: No Earth contact at end: first contact 2029-07-24T12:00:00 UTC, longest blackout 19 h.
2 dark spells, the longest 14 h; the battery lasts through every one, at best (sun-tracking panels).
With half the battery it dies at hour 295 (2029-08-05T19 UTC), even at best (sun-tracking panels).

checks: Sun and Earth positions: 124 checked against NASA JPL Horizons, all within 0.0003 deg.
Sunlight: matches NASA's PGDA map at the Shackleton rim, correlation 0.92 (2 m best fit).
cannot_see: Hazards smaller than the 20 m map, like the ~20 m crater IM-2 tipped into.
A tilted lander with fixed panels, like IM-1: survival here is an upper bound.

nasa_check.how: Open a link: NASA JPL Horizons lists azimuth and elevation in degrees at this site and hour; compare its elevation with ours (Horizons' azimuth is clockwise from north).

words: Land up to 11 h late and it is still safe on the exact point (no date here is safe if the lander misses by 100 m); a 24 h slip is not: the next safe hour is 2029-08-22T09 UTC.
Missed by up to 100 m: 3 of 17 points safe; at the point 50 m toward bearing 242 deg, its ground slopes 10.0 deg over 100 m.
